name: Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As
nameAr: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص بن وائل بن هاشم بن سعيد بن سعد بن سهم القرشي السهمي رضي الله عنهما

orthography.spelled: In his nasab, Su'ayd ibn Sa'd ibn Sahm is a diminutive, with dammah on the sin and fathah on the ayn (Taqrib; al-Nawawi).

diedNote: Taqrib: in Dhu al-Hijjah, on the nights of al-Harrah (63 AH) on the sounder view, at al-Ta'if on the preferable view. Other reports: 65 (Yahya ibn Bukayr, al-Waqidi, Khalifah), 67 aged 72, 68 (al-Layth), 73, 77; and the place Makkah, Egypt or Palestine.

deathVariants.authority: Ahmad ibn Hanbal ("the nights of al-Harrah"); Ibn Hajar, Taqrib
Yahya ibn Bukayr; al-Waqidi; Khalifah ibn Khayyat

taqrib.ar: أحد السابقين المكثرين من الصحابة وأحد العبادلة الفقهاء، مات في ذي الحجة ليالي الحرة على الأصح بالطائف على الراجح
taqrib.en: One of the early converts and prolific narrators among the Companions, and one of the four Abdullahs who were jurists; he died in Dhu al-Hijjah on the nights of al-Harrah on the sounder view, at al-Ta'if on the preferable view.

flags.label: Few narrators despite much hadith
flags.detail: Al-Nawawi explains that although he carried a great deal, relatively little was transmitted from him because he settled in Egypt, to which few travelled, unlike Abu Hurayrah in Madinah (Tahdhib al-Asma' 1/282). Abu Hurayrah himself said no one had more hadith from the Prophet than he, except Abdullah ibn Amr, who wrote while Abu Hurayrah did not (Tahdhib al-Kamal 15/358).

flags.label: Age gap with his father
flags.detail: Only eleven years separated him from his father Amr ibn al-As (Tahdhib al-Kamal 15/358); al-Nawawi gives twelve, or eleven.

flags.label: Shamela record
flags.detail: Shamela's narrator index has no working page for him (entry 3819 is blank); the Tahdhib al-Kamal pages are cited directly.

bio: A Companion and the son of the Companion Amr ibn al-As, born only eleven years after his father and converted before him; one of the four Abdullahs (al-Abadilah) whose agreement in law carried weight, with Ibn Umar, Ibn Abbas and Ibn al-Zubayr, as Ahmad and the hadith scholars named them. He wrote hadith down, which Abu Hurayrah cited as the one reason anyone had more than he did, said he had memorised a thousand parables from the Prophet ﷺ, carried his father's banner at Yarmuk and settled in Egypt. Al-Nawawi dwells on his eminence, jurisprudence, abundant hadith, scrupulousness and devotion to prayer and fasting. He died on the nights of al-Harrah or soon after; al-Ta'if, Makkah, Egypt and Palestine are all named as the place.
